prompts.Left:
Use case: precise-object-edit, identity-preserve. Edit Image1, an atlas of the user's EXISTING white bichon desktop pet. Image2 is ONLY a four-paw motion diagram, not a character reference. Output exactly the same 1536x1024, 4 columns x 2 rows, eight chronological cells 0,1,2,3 / 4,5,6,7, real RGBA transparent background.
Keep the original large round head, exact three-quarter face toward viewer, floppy long ear hair, happy open mouth and pink tongue, white curly coat, compact short body, red patterned collar and gold bell, rounded curled fluffy tail. Retain head/body size, angle and position consistently in ALL eight cells. This must look like the same original pet, not a different realistic dog. Change ONLY four legs below the fixed shoulder/hip roots. Clean true alpha outside silhouettes, no stray dots, floor, shadow, checkerboard, labels or colored lines.
Follow every cell in Image2: dark blue = near foreleg, dark green = near hindleg, pale blue = far foreleg, pale green = far hindleg. Solid paw dot = ground support; hollow dot = lifted. Trace each leg from its own fixed root; do not swap near/far ownership. The diagram already uses the original pet's compact proportions. Keep short fluffy legs, natural canine elbows, knees and backwards hocks beneath fur; avoid stiff straight rods or excessive backward kicking.
CRITICAL corrected sequence: Near fore paw extends/lands0, stays planted and progresses smoothly backward1,2,3,4 WITHOUT reversing forward or lifting early; lifts/bends5, swings low forward6, reaches forward near ground7, then lands0. Near hind supports and travels backward0,1,2,3, begins small toe-off4 while the near fore is STILL planted, folds and brings paw forward underneath hip5, lands slightly forward6, supports7 then0. Far hind lifts0, recovers1, lands2, supports3,4,5,6,7. Far fore supports0, lifts1, swings2, reaches3, lands4, supports5,6,7. Four beats, continuous ground support; never put both forelegs or both hindlegs in the same pose. Keep all four paw paths legible, with natural occlusion, no merged blobs.
Prioritize exact diagram paw LOCATION and contact state, especially near fore3 and4 remaining BACK and on ground, and near hind4->5->6 curling forward and lowering, not teleporting. A supported paw never slides forward relative to the torso before toe-off. Render one continuous repeatable walk-in-place cycle, modest stride and low clearance, not eight unrelated static poses. Last cell7 and first0 must be adjacent walk phases.
Direction LEFT only. Preserve the exact left-facing face in Image1; no mirrored new head, no yaw or change of expression.
